The new receipt email is now behind a flag. One problem: the new email itself doesn't exist in the repo yet, so the flag currently switches to a template that isn't there.

**What changed** (`services/notifier/notifier/email.py`):
- `send_receipt` uses the `receipt_v2` template when `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2=1`. Otherwise it keeps using `receipt`.
- I used an environment variable instead of `flags.is_on()` / `flags.toml`. The notifier is deployed on its own and can't read the root `flags.toml`, so its flags are `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` environment variables set to `"1"`.
- The flag is checked on every send, so you can turn it on or off by changing the function's environment, with no code change.
- Any value other than `"1"` (including `"true"`) leaves the flag off.

**Tests** (`tests/test_email.py`): I added cases for flag on, flag off and a non-`"1"` value. All 3 tests pass.

**Before you turn the flag on:**
- There's no `services/notifier/templates/` directory and no `receipt_v2` template. `render()` is also still a `NotImplementedError` stub.
- You'll need to add `templates/receipt_v2.mjml` and a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` with the same variables (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`). If the new email lives on another branch or uses a different template name, tell me and I'll point the flag at it.
- "Gradually" here means per deployment: the flag is on or off for a whole environment. Rolling out to a share of customers would need a hash of the customer id checked against a rollout percentage. I can add that if you want it.

I haven't committed anything.
